input: What is the standard procedure for an underway replenishment (UNREP)?
golden: 1) The receiving ship and supply ship coordinate a rendezvous and matching course/speed; 2) A line is passed between the ships to establish a connection; 3) Fuel hoses or cargo rigs are rigged between the vessels; 4) Fuel, stores, or ammunition are transferred while underway; 5) Rigs are disconnected once transfer is complete; 6) Ships separate to a safe distance.

input: What is the standard procedure for helicopter operations aboard a ship (flight quarters)?

input: What is the standard procedure for a watch turnover between two sailors?
golden: 1) The oncoming watchstander reports early and reviews the current status; 2) The offgoing watchstander briefs all pertinent information, including any ongoing issues; 3) Equipment readings and logs are reviewed together; 4) The oncoming watchstander verifies understanding and asks questions; 5) The oncoming watchstander formally relieves the watch by stating 'I relieve you'; 6) The offgoing watchstander confirms and departs.

input: What is the standard general quarters (battle stations) procedure when the alarm sounds?
golden: 1) The general alarm sounds throughout the ship; 2) All personnel proceed immediately to their assigned general quarters stations; 3) Watertight doors and hatches are closed to set material condition Zebra; 4) Stations report manned and ready to the bridge/combat systems; 5) The ship prepares to respond to the threat or drill scenario; 6) General quarters is secured once the situation is resolved.

input: What is the standard procedure for a medical emergency aboard a ship at sea?
golden: 1) The sailor reports the emergency to the corpsman/medical department and the bridge; 2) Basic first aid is administered immediately by nearby personnel; 3) The patient is moved to sick bay for further treatment; 4) The medical team assesses whether the case requires evacuation; 5) If needed, a medical evacuation (MEDEVAC) is coordinated, often by helicopter; 6) The incident is documented in the medical log.

input: What is the standard procedure for towing a disabled ship?
golden: 1) The towing ship approaches the disabled vessel and establishes communication; 2) A messenger line is passed, followed by the main towing hawser; 3) The tow line is secured to strong points on both ships; 4) The towing ship takes up slack gradually and begins towing at low speed; 5) Both crews monitor the tow line tension and course throughout; 6) The tow is released once the disabled ship reaches port or assistance arrives.

input: What is the standard procedure for a ship entering a foreign port for a scheduled visit?
golden: 1) Diplomatic clearance is obtained in advance from the host nation; 2) The ship coordinates a pilot for the approach if required; 3) Customs, immigration, and quarantine formalities are completed on arrival; 4) The ship moors or anchors as directed by port authorities; 5) Official calls are made between the ship's command and local officials; 6) Liberty and port visit activities begin per the ship's schedule.

input: What is the standard procedure for conducting a damage control drill (fire and flooding combined scenario)?
golden: 1) A scenario is announced (e.g., simulated fire and flooding in a compartment); 2) Repair parties muster and respond to the simulated casualty; 3) Teams practice setting boundaries, fighting the simulated fire, and controlling simulated flooding; 4) An evaluator observes and times the response; 5) The space is reset to normal condition; 6) A critique is held to identify lessons learned.

input: What is the standard procedure for a ship conducting a security alert boarding of a suspicious vessel?
golden: 1) The ship hails the suspicious vessel and requests identification; 2) If warranted, a boarding team is prepared and briefed; 3) The boarding team approaches by small boat and boards the vessel safely; 4) The team inspects cargo, documents, and crew as authorized; 5) Findings are reported back to the ship; 6) The vessel is released, detained, or escorted based on the findings.

input: What is the standard procedure for securing a ship's engineering plant after returning to port?
golden: 1) The engineering officer of the watch is notified of the plan to secure; 2) Non-essential systems are shut down in a controlled sequence; 3) Shore power and services are connected as needed; 4) Remaining equipment is placed in standby or secured status; 5) Logs are completed noting the final status of all systems; 6) The watch is reduced to an in-port duty section.
